CALIBRATION

I built a CIFAR-10 classifier that knows when it doesn't know — unsure pictures go to a human.

45.31% · 3,833 auto at 61.07% ★ Featured · Nov 2026
GitHub ↗Details →

Calibration — CIFAR-10 Classifier with Human Review

I trained a CIFAR-10 classifier — ResNet18 with a frozen backbone and a new Linear(512, 10) head (5,130 trainable parameters), head-only for 3 epochs — then added a calibration layer: predictions below 0.50 confidence go to a human for review instead of a confident wrong guess.

  • Overall test accuracy 45.31% (4,531 / 10,000); weakest class cat at 184, best ship at 522
  • At 0.50 it auto-decides 3,833 pictures at 61.07% accuracy and sends 6,167 to a human; those labels are saved for a future batch retrain
  • When a human saves a label it replies: “Got it, thanks for the review — I'm still learning.”
  • Honest limit: CIFAR-10 has only 10 classes — a picture outside them is force-guessed; there is no out-of-distribution check yet

NEURALSTREAM

I built a two-tower neural retrieval system over a 1M-item catalog.

sub-50ms p95 · 1M items
GitHub ↗Details →

Neural Retrieval & Ranking System

I built a two-tower PyTorch network that embeds users and items into a shared 64-D space. I indexed the precomputed embeddings with an exact FAISS flat inner-product index, so it returns top-K results from a 1M-item catalog at sub-50ms p95, served through FastAPI.

  • I trained v1 on positives only (ratings 4+)
  • I evaluate head and tail items separately, as my guard against popularity bias
  • I verified the index results score-for-score against PyTorch ground truth

I validate every query before it runs

Autonomous Multi-Agent Data Intelligence

I built this as a LangGraph multi-agent system over DuckDB: my agents plan, write, validate, and visualize SQL end to end — question in, chart out — with Llama 3.3 (Groq) as the model layer.

  • My critic agent catches hallucinated or invalid SQL before anything runs
  • When validation fails, the system retries within a bounded limit
  • The full path runs question → validated SQL → chart

INVENTORY & DEMAND FORECAST

I forecast demand and planned replenishment across 20 SKUs and 3 warehouses.

98.92% fill rate · 1,853 units
GitHub ↗Details →

Demand Planning Analysis

I forecast demand across 20 SKUs × 3 warehouses over 365 days of daily demand (218,146 units total; seeded simulated data, which I label as such in the project). I ran the analysis in SQL (6 queries), built the forecast in Python (moving average and exponential smoothing, median MAPE 22.16% on a last-30-days holdout), modeled it in Excel (5 sheets), and finished with a 17-row recommendations action table.

  • I measured a 98.92% fill rate across the network
  • I caught a Wireless Mouse promo stockout: 20 days, 1,511 unfilled — and recommended ordering 724 units
  • I flagged Bluetooth Speaker Mini as dead stock (SKU-203, $11,724.90) and recommended stopping replenishment
  • My recommended orders total 1,853 units across 16 SKUs
